method: Production player movement with actual OBB contacts and geometry fixtures for thin walls, corners, curbs, stairs, ledges, jump/ceiling, dynamic supports, teleports, timing, and current authored city bins.

results.test: Eye height follows real raised pavement and remains grounded while idle
Acceleration, sprint, diagonal normalization, braking, and frame-rate consistency
High-speed dash cannot tunnel through a25mm-thick wall
Rotated OBB collision preserves tangential movement for smooth wall sliding
Two perpendicular walls resolve a corner without jitter or penetration
Real curb tops raise feet and descending curbs settle without hovering
Sequential20cm stairs climb using real tops and stop floating when the stairs end
A50cm ledge blocks walking but can be jumped onto and supports landing
Jump uses pavement height, cannot double jump, and lands without falling through
A low ceiling stops the head instead of allowing an upward clip
Walking off a tall platform causes a real fall and gravity remains active during air dashes
Dynamic props block walking; removed support causes a fall on the next update
External teleport clears old velocity and never sweeps across the intervening world
World bounds and large frame gaps stay bounded; collider queries are shared by substeps
The current authored city sidewalk and actual extracted bin stop the player at the visible footprint
